faq.question: How much is the rooftop solar subsidy in 2026?
faq.answer: The central subsidy is ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the third, up to ₹78,000. In Tamil Nadu, the state adds ₹5,000, ₹10,000 or ₹22,000 for 1, 2 or 3 kW, for a total of up to ₹1 lakh.

faq.question: How many units does a 3 kW solar system produce?
faq.answer: About 4,200 units a year, or roughly 690 units every two months, in most of India. Actual output depends on your roof direction, shading, dust and season, and falls slightly as panels age.

faq.question: Will my electricity bill become zero with solar?
faq.answer: It can if your system produces as much as your net use, but fixed or meter charges may remain. In Tamil Nadu, households using under 500 units every two months already get 200 units free, so they only need enough solar to cover the units above that.

faq.question: Is rooftop solar worth it for a small household?
faq.answer: Often not, where low usage is already free or cheap. In our Tamil Nadu example, a 300-unit household would take about 16 years to recover the cost of even a 1 kW system after subsidies. Households with large bills recover the cost far faster.

faq.question: Do I need DCR panels to get the subsidy?
faq.answer: Yes. The PM Surya Ghar subsidy applies to systems using domestically manufactured (DCR) panels installed by a registered vendor. Non-DCR systems can still be installed and net-metered, but without the subsidy.
